## A Room Lit by One Lamp

The universe is too easily imagined as a room already lit from every
side. Every object is there. Every coordinate is written. Every observer
is placed on the same floor plan. Consciousness then becomes a person
inside the room, walking around with a lantern.

BEDC begins with a smaller and stricter image.

There is a lamp. The lamp does not illuminate the whole world. It
illuminates what has become record for one focused history. The room
available to this lamp is not the total room from nowhere. It is the
lit surface, the retained trace, the shadows with provenance, the
relations to other lamps, and the honest boundary where light stops.

The local universe is not unreal. It is local.

## The Universe-for-a-Focus

A focused ledger does not carry the universe itself. It carries a
finite packet:

histories, continuation traces, selector rows, compression residues,
relation witnesses, invariant rows, and an audit row refusing hidden
global supply.

This packet can be read as the universe for the focus. Not because it
contains everything, but because it contains everything this focus can
read as displayed, transported, compressed with provenance, or marked
as boundary.

A map without a border is mythology. A map with a border is useful.
The border does not say the land ends there. It says the map ends
there.

## The Reading Self

Consciousness is often made too large or too small. Too large: it is
treated as a substance outside the records, a hidden monarch behind the
world. Too small: it is treated as one object among objects, as if a
brain scan should find it like a coin under a stone.

BEDC reads consciousness as focused readback. A history reaches an
endpoint, carries its trace, selects what enters focus, and exposes a
self-proxy. The self is not an extra tenant in the ledger. It is the
ledger reading itself at a local endpoint.

A whirlpool is not outside the river. It is a place where the river
locally folds, gathers, and makes its own motion visible. Consciousness
is like that: not a second river and not the source of all water, but a
focused event in which flow becomes locally readable.

## Other Histories

Other minds are not solved by entering another interior. They are not
solved by declaring every behavior to be mere exterior. They are
approached through relation rows.

Another history appears through behavior, communication, shared events,
correction, refusal, coordination, and locality cells. The evidence is
finite. The commitment that the other is another inscription-bearing
history is not reducible to one private representation.

Two lamps can illuminate the same table from different sides. Their
shadows differ. Their records differ. Yet the table can become stable
through relation: paired marks, transport, comparison, repeated
correction, and gap honesty.

Objectivity begins there: not in a god's-eye view, but in the
discipline by which local views become mutually answerable without
ceasing to be local.

## Why This Matters

The old metaphysical temptation is to close too much. Make the universe
a total object. Make consciousness a hidden substance. Make other minds
directly readable. Make time a single global clock. Make death the
death of being. Make love fusion.

BEDC refuses these closures not because it wants mystery, but because
it wants exactness. Each refusal protects a distinction:

the local universe is not the total universe;
the conscious carrier is not $\mathsf{T}$;
the other history is not my representation;
formal continuation is not embodied continuation;
relation is not fusion.

The world does not become poorer when these distinctions are kept. It
becomes less dishonest. The lamp is finite, but its finite light can be
clean.

## Strict Mathematical Form

Let a finite focused multi-Hist ledger be
$$
\mathcal{L}_N=(I,H,\Theta,F,S,D,G,R,J,Q,\rho,A).
$$

Here $I$ is a finite displayed index ledger, $H(i)\in\Hist$ is the
history at index $i$, $\Theta(i)$ is its local $\Cont$ trace, $F\in I$
is the focus row, $S$ is the selector ledger, $D,G$ are digest and
gap/provenance rows, $R$ is the inter-$\Hist$ relation ledger, $J$ is
the invariant ledger, $Q$ is a finite dependence ledger, $\rho$ is the
self-proxy, and $A$ is the audit row.

Define the conscious record:
$$
\operatorname{ConsciousRecord}(\mathcal{L}_N,F)
:=
(H(F),\Theta(F),S(F),\rho).
$$

Define the finite universe-for-the-focus:
$$
\operatorname{Universe}_{\mathcal{L}_N,F}
:=
(I,H,\Theta,S,D,G,R,J,Q,F).
$$

The records-side closure condition is:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ClosedLedger}(\mathcal{L}_N)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{Generated}(H)
\wedge
\operatorname{SelectorLedgered}(S)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{GapAccounted}(G)
\wedge
\operatorname{RelationWitnessed}(R)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{InvariantStable}(J)
\wedge
\operatorname{AuditRefusal}(A).
\end{aligned}
$$

For another index $j\in I$, define local otherness:
$$
\operatorname{OtherHist}_{F}(j)
\Longleftrightarrow
j\in I
\wedge
\neg\hsame(H(F),H(j)).
$$

Define a locality cell between $F$ and $j$ for an event row $e$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{LocalityCell}_{F,j}(e)
\Longleftrightarrow{}&
\operatorname{RecordFrom}(H(F),e_F)
\wedge
\operatorname{RecordFrom}(H(j),e_j)\\
&{}\wedge
\operatorname{GapOrProvenance}(e_F,e_j)
\wedge
\operatorname{HsameStable}(e_F,e_j).
\end{aligned}
$$

The non-collapse laws are:
$$
\operatorname{Universe}_{\mathcal{L}_N,F}
\not\equiv
\text{the universe itself},
$$

$$
\operatorname{ConsciousRecord}(\mathcal{L}_N,F)
\not\equiv
\mathsf{T},
$$

$$
\operatorname{OtherHist}_{F}(j)
\not\equiv
\operatorname{Representation}_{F}(j),
$$

$$
\operatorname{LocalityCell}_{F,j}(e)
\not\Rightarrow
\text{global frame}.
$$

The strict summary is:
$$
\text{closed records-side world}
=
\text{finite generated ledger}
+
\text{local focus}
+
\text{witnessed relations}
+
\text{honest boundary}.
$$
